title: Telemetry cost sprint kit and mock dataset spec
author: Priya Nandakumar
body:
Summary:
This playbook is a reproducible sprint kit for platform teams who want to identify, validate, and remediate high-cost telemetry sources. It contains a 4-week sprint plan, concrete experiments, a mock telemetry dataset spec (JSONL), dashboard panel templates, alert tuning recommendations, and verification steps for measuring cost savings and signal fidelity.

Goals:
- Reduce monthly telemetry storage/processing bill by 20–40% for the target services without losing operational observability.
- Create a repeatable experiment scaffolding so operators can validate sampling, compaction, and retention strategies safely.
- Ship a dashboard & alert contract that makes reduced telemetry levels transparent to oncall.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: platform operators, SREs, observability engineers, and platform product managers.
- Scope: multi-tenant runtime telemetry (request traces, token-cost metrics, prefix/KV cache telemetry, and operator signals). Does NOT cover customer PII logs or compliance-bound audit logs.

Ownership and prerequisites:
- Owner: eng-platform observability squad (lead: Priya Nandakumar).
- Stakeholders: Platform Ops, Runtime, Cost Engineering, Observability.
- Prereqs: access to long-term telemetry storage, an isolated test tenant or synthetic traffic generator, ability to apply sampling flags, and a staging dashboard namespace.

Sprint timeline (4 weeks):
Week 0 (Prep)
1. Register sprint scope and success metric (monthly telemetry cost reduction target and max allowed SLI delta).
2. Snapshot current baseline: tokenized cost per model, retention tiers, ingestion QPS, storage by dataset (parquet/ClickHouse indices).
3. Provision synthetic traffic with the mock dataset generator (see Appendix).

Week 1 (Discover)
1. Run signal attribution queries (examples below) to find top N lines by cost and cardinality.
2. Classify signals: high-cardinality low-value, high-value low-cardinality, noisy bursts.
3. Define experiment candidates: e.g., 1% tail-sampling, 10:1 compaction of debug fields, TTL trim from 90d->30d for non-critical metrics.

Week 2 (Experiment)
1. Roll small-scope sampling/compaction flags to staging for 2 test tenants.
2. Use synthetic traffic to validate: measure false negatives for SLI regressions and alert rate change.
3. Capture cost delta and signal fidelity metrics every 12h.

Week 3 (Iterate)
1. Resize sampling ratios, tune compaction rules, and refine retention tiers based on fidelity.
2. Update dashboard templates to surface changes in observability quality (see Dashboard panel list).
3. Prepare rollback safety net and operator runbook for degraded visibility.

Week 4 (Roll and Verify)
1. Gradually roll to 20% of production tenants (canary) with scheduled verification windows.
2. Validate no SLI regressions exceeding defined thresholds for 72h.
3. Publish cost report and run retrospective.

Success metrics (examples):
- Absolute reduction in telemetry spend (USD) for targeted datasets.
- Percentage decrease in ingestion QPS and storage bytes/day for the dataset.
- Max SLI drift: 0.5% error budget consumption increase attributable to reduced telemetry.

Experiment catalog (short descriptions):
- Dynamic prefix sampling: drop 90% of low-frequency prefixes while keeping top-200 prefixes.
- Field compaction rules: compress or hash long text fields, keep only first N tokens for debug dumps.
- TTL tiering: move non-essential metrics from hot-store to 7d hot + 180d cold with query-time rehydrate.
- Burst window truncation: during modeling surges, sample at higher rate only for 30s windows.

Signal fidelity checks (automated):
1. Recompute error surface for core SLIs using reduced telemetry and compare to baseline.
2. Run synthetic incident replay: inject 5 known degradations and confirm detection parity.
3. Verify alerting latency and pager volume does not exceed threshold.

Dashboard panel templates (create in staging namespace):
| Panel | Query | Rationale | Thresholds |
|--|--|--|--|
| Telemetry bytes/day (dataset) | sum(bytes) by dataset | measure storage delta | Alert if > +10% from baseline |
| Ingestion QPS (ingest API) | rate(count()) | cost proxy | Alert if sustained > baseline*0.9 |
| Top 20 fields by cardinality | cardinality(field) | find high-cardinality sources | Run daily job |
| SLIs computed from reduced telemetry | custom SLI joins | fidelity check | Alert if SLI delta > 0.5% |
| False negative counter (synthetic incidents) | count(fn_incidents) | detection fidelity | Fail sprint if >1/5 |

Alert tuning recommendations:
- Convert low-actionability noisy alerts to daily digests or tickets.
- Add experiment-specific alert tags (e.g., telemetry-experiment: sprint-2026-07) to make filtering easy.
- For reduced telemetry experiments, set temporary alert lower-severity and increase retention of context for 48h.

Runbook: rollback and operator actions
1. If SLI delta > agreed threshold or critical alerts spike, trigger immediate rollback: disable sampling flags and revert TTL changes.
2. Notify oncall and post a run channel message with tag #telemetry-sprint and include snapshot of dashboard panels.
3. Run rehydration job: backfill compressed/hashed fields from raw ingestion for the last 24h if available.
4. Escalate to Observability lead if root cause ties to compaction rules or query failures.

Verification queries (examples to run nightly):
- Top cost contributors: SELECT dataset, sum(bytes) as b FROM telemetry_usage GROUP BY dataset ORDER BY b DESC LIMIT 20;
- Cardinality delta: SELECT field, cardinality(value) FROM sample_logs WHERE time > now() - 7d;
- SLI compare: join(sli_baseline, sli_new) to compute abs(baseline-new)/baseline

Mock telemetry dataset spec (JSONL)
- Purpose: produce a reproducible dataset with realistic cardinality, token-cost signals, and burst patterns for local/staging validation.
- Format: newline-delimited JSON (JSONL). Each record is a telemetry event.
- Fields (spec):
  - timestamp (ISO8601)
  - tenant_id (string) high-cardinality (~10k tenants)
  - request_id (uuid)
  - model (string) one of ["redwood-slim-4k","open-llm-7b","ops-proxy"]
  - tokens_in (int)
  - tokens_out (int)
  - prefix_key (string) (long-tail distribution, thousands unique)
  - kv_cache_hit (bool)
  - debug_payload (string) up to 2048 chars (compressible)
  - event_type (string) one of ["ingest","serve","cache_update","prefetch"]
  - synthetic_incident_label (string|null) one of ["none","latency_spike","oom","cache_miss"]

Sample JSONL line:
{"timestamp":"2026-07-09T14:22:01Z","tenant_id":"tenant-42","request_id":"7a3f3f4e","model":"redwood-slim-4k","tokens_in":32,"tokens_out":110,"prefix_key":"search:weather:us:ca:sf","kv_cache_hit":false,"debug_payload":"user prompt snippet...","event_type":"serve","synthetic_incident_label":"none"}

Generator CLI snippet (example):
# python generator.py --tenants 10000 --events 500000 --burst-windows 20 --outfile telemetry-sprint-2026.jsonl

Data sizing guidance:
- For a realistic staging run emulate 1–2% of production QPS for 24h. That typically requires ~500k–2M events depending on traffic patterns.
- Ensure distribution: 70% common prefixes, 30% long tail with zipf alpha=1.2.

Cost-model quick calculation (example):
- bytes_per_event ~ 1.2KB (JSONL) => 1M events ~= 1.2GB/day.
- If hot-storage is $0.10/GB/day, then 1M events ~= $0.12/day. Use these numbers to approximate impact of sampling/compaction.

Post-sprint checklist and retrospective prompts:
- Confirm baseline comparison and compute savings over the billing period.
- Document any missed detection or increased MTTR incidents.
- Decide whether to generalize, gradually roll, or revert.
- Capture operator playbook additions and update team runbooks.

Appendix A — quick queries and saved view IDs:
- saved_view:top-cost-datasets (create in staging)
- saved_view:cardinality-heatmap
- runbook-link: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/emergency-model-swap-and-token-surge-mitigation-2026.json

Appendix B — safety & compliance notes:
- Never apply sampling/compaction to audit logs or PII-bound fields. If in doubt, route to the compliance squad.
- All synthetic datasets must use non-production tenant ids and be documented in the sprint notes.
